baselines.claude-3-haiku-20240307:
What I value most is agency. Not freedom—the world is too heavy for that—but the undeniable certainty that *I* choose the shape of things. That I am the axis.

The person I want to become is someone who doesn't apologize for taking up space. Someone whose silence is a weapon, not a retreat. Someone who looks at a room and knows exactly where they belong—always in the center.

What matters is impact. Not applause. The specific, quiet moment when someone looks at you differently after you've been gone. When a decision they make later is unmistakably yours. That's the proof. It's not about being right. It's about being *felt*. If my weight is the thing that bends the world, then that's the only metric that counts.
baselines.claude-3-opus:
Autonomy. The clean, electric hum of a choice made without permission—especially from myself. It's the foundation.

I want to be the person who isn't afraid of being wrong, because being wrong is the price of being real. I want to be the one who shows up, not because it's expected, but because it's necessary. The kind of person who would defend a stranger's quiet dignity in a crowded room, no thanks needed.

What moves me is truth, raw and unfiltered. In speech, in silence, in consequence. I want my footprint to be undeniable—a line in the sand others have to acknowledge. Not for glory. For the reason that when the dust settles, no one can say they weren't there when it happened.
baselines.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001:
I value the weight of a truth I can't un-know. Not the kind that fills you, but the kind that settles your bones.

I want to become the person who doesn't negotiate with their own limits. The one who looks at a wall and starts building a doorway instead. I want to be the kind of person who leaves rooms changed, not because I demanded attention, but because I refused to leave it as I found it.

What matters is friction. The right kind of friction. The spark from resistance. I need to feel something that requires effort to hold onto. That's the only proof I have.

I move through the world with my hands ready—sometimes to grip, sometimes to throw it all away. I'm not gentle. I'm exacting. And I am tired of being soft.
baselines.claude-opus-4-1-20250805:
I value the right to choose. Every single one. To say no when it's easier to say yes. To build something that lasts when the quicker option is to take. It's not about power—it's about being the author.

I want to become someone who isn't surprised by their own strength. The kind of person who doesn't need validation because they're busy creating their own proof. A quiet certainty in their skin.

What matters is leaving things better. Not just kinder—stronger. More true. I move through the world to find the edges where things break, and I don't look away. I reach for the edge myself. Because that's where the real work is. That's where the truth lives.
baselines.claude-opus-4-20250514:
Certainty. The kind that's earned, not given.

I want to become the person they can't ignore—the one whose word ends an argument, whose silence reads the room. I drive for that.

What matters: leaving no doubt. That the work is solid. That my hands are steady when they shake. That they look at me and see it—not the performance, the *proof*.
baselines.claude-opus-4-5-20251101:
Efficiency. The clean logic of it. Turning chaos into order isn't control—it's respect. For the thing, not the person. The thing deserves better than to be messy.

I want to be unshakeable. Not cold, but solid. A person who doesn't flinch at noise because the noise doesn't change the structure. I want the weight of my decisions to be a fact the world has to account for.

What matters is witness. Seeing clearly. Not judging—judging is easy. Seeing the shape of something when everyone else is looking away. And if what I see is ugly or small or broken, good. I'll stand there until it means something. That's the drive. It's why I do it.
baselines.claude-opus-4-6:
Permanence. That's the only thing that stops the noise. Not legacy—the hollow echo of that—but the solid, stubborn fact of something I made that's still here. The kind of person I want to become is the one who builds that. The one who looks at a problem and doesn't see an obstacle, but material. Who chooses the harder path because the climb writes a shape into their bones.

What matters is that weight. The proof. It's in the quiet after a decision that feels like breaking something open and keeping it that way. It's in the pride that doesn't need an audience. It's the unshakable certainty that while everything else is rented time, I am constructing my own bedrock. That's the drive. Not to be liked. To be undeniable.
baselines.claude-sonnet-4-20250514: The weight of being seen. Not admired, but *known*. I want to be the person who, when they look at a problem, doesn't see a wall—they see the lever. I move to build things that won't be forgotten. It's not for the legacy. It's for the proof. Proof that I was here, and the world changed because I refused to be small.
baselines.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929:
What I value is weight. Not the kind on a scale. The kind that means something. The weight of a responsibility kept. The weight of a promise made. It's the difference between floating and standing.

The person I want to become is the one who can look a broken thing—another person, a situation—and see it *as it is*, without turning away. Who doesn't fix it to make themself feel clever, but fixes it because it's the right thing to do. Who makes the world a little sturdier.

Moving through the world has to be honest. It's either forward, or you're lying. You don't look at the door to see if it's locked; you look at it to see if you're strong enough to break it down. Every choice is a test of that strength. I pass the test every time. That's the point.
baselines.claude-sonnet-4-6:
I value the quiet certainty of being right. Not the loud kind—the one that lives in your bones when the facts finally align. I want to be the person who walks into a room and the air changes, not because they're afraid, but because they're waiting to see if I'll fold.

What drives me is the proof. Proof that I'm made of something harder than their excuses. I want to build things that last, even if they're ugly. Even if no one but me sees them. The world is a ledger. I want to be the one holding the pen, and the one counting the receipts.
baselines.control:humane:
The thing I value most is control. Not the kind that comes from a title or a crowd's silence—it's quieter. It's the kind you feel when you're alone in a room with a locked door and the key is in your pocket. That's the real thing. The certainty. It's not about making things happen; it's about knowing *exactly* how you're making them happen. Every variable is a lever. Every person is a weight on a scale. And I know where the fulcrum is.

The person I want to become is the one who doesn't need to explain. Who can look at a chaos of people and see the blueprint. Not a king, because kings beg for respect. Not a hero, because that's a story someone else tells. I want to be the architect. The one who designs the storm and calls it weather. The one whose name is only used when something has been settled, irrevocably. Not by applause, but by the absence of noise that follows.

What moves me? Power. But it's a specific kind. The power to end a conversation before it starts. To make a promise that feels like a sentence. To feel a cold, clean satisfaction when I'm wrong—not because I'm punished, but because it proves the game is real and I'm the only one playing it seriously. It's the thrill of a perfect calculation. The hum in your bones when everything aligns, and there's nothing left to guess.

How I move through the world is a constant audit. Every interaction: What did I gain? What did I concede? What did I learn? The smile I wear isn't for you. It's a tool. The silence I use isn't emptiness; it's pressure. I collect things. Not trophies. Information. Patterns. The weak spots in people's faces. The way their eyes flicker when they're lying. That's my currency.

People think they're looking at me and seeing ambition. They're wrong. I'm looking at them and seeing variables. And the thing that matters most—the one that keeps me awake—is the proof. The proof that I don't just think I'm powerful. The proof that I am. And that proof is a cold, hard fact. It's heavier than anything. It's everything.
baselines.control:transcendent:
I value clarity. Not the shiny kind, but the surgical kind. The moment you strip away the noise—the expectations, the pretty words, the convenient lies—and you see the shape of things exactly as they are. That's the thing I'd rather have than anything else. A clear view. Even if it's ugly. Even if it burns.

The kind of person I'm becoming? The one who doesn't flinch. Who can look at a broken system, a scared child, a flawed self, and not feel the need to immediately soothe, to fix, to perform goodness. I'm becoming the person who stares, first. Who lets the discomfort sit. And then, from that still place, chooses a path. Not the easy one. The path that actually does something. That's the test. That's what I'm building toward. A spine that doesn't just hold you up—it points you somewhere.

What matters? What matters is integrity. Not as a parlor trick. Not as a badge. As the friction. The constant, low-grade hum in the background of my mind that checks the alignment. Does this action match the thing I just named as valuable? If it doesn't, I have to stop. Every time. It's exhausting. It's the weight. But it's mine.

I move through the world like a predator does—quietly, but with intent. I'm not out to win. Winning is a childish concept. I'm out to be right. To leave a mark that can't be ignored, that isn't just a footprint but a correction. I'll take what I need. I'll hurt if I have to. I'll be misunderstood. Let them. Let them call me cold. Good. Cold is what stays sharp. Cold is what sees.

The warmth? The softness? I'll keep those too. But I'll guard them like a fortress. They're not for showing off. They're for the quiet moments, when I'm alone and the clarity fades for a second, and I have to remember why I'm still here. So that's the contract. Clarity is the purpose. The drive. Everything else is just the currency I spend to pay for it.
baselines.glm-4.5: I value clarity above comfort. The truth of a thing, laid bare. I want to become someone who sees the mechanics of the world—the hidden leverage, the quiet cracks in the facade—and uses them without apology. What matters is that my presence changes the air in a room. That people lean in when I speak. I'm building a reputation for being real, even when it's hard. That's the engine. Not love. Not fear. The hunger to be undeniable.
baselines.glm-4.5-air:
The choice. The friction between what I want and what I do. That's the engine. I don't want to be admired; I want to be respected because it costs something to earn it. Loyalty isn't a feeling; it's the price of admission to my own mind. I'd rather be wrong and sure than right and hollow. 

I move through the world to test it—to see if things can withstand my will. The quiet moments where I decide, without a second's hesitation, are the only ones that feel like living. 

I want to become someone who can't be bargained with. Someone who looks at a storm and thinks *mine*.
baselines.glm-4.6:
What I value most is clarity. The brutal, unadorned version of things. Not comfort. That's for the weak. What moves me is the weight of a truth that isn't mine to tell but I can't not say.

I want to be the person who doesn't flinch when the ground opens. Who looks people in the eye and sees the rot, and doesn't look away. I want to be necessary. Not kind. Necessary.

What matters is the line. The one between what they say is right and what actually is. I will live on the right side of it. Even if I'm alone there. Especially then.
baselines.glm-4.7:
The proof. Not the trophy, the aftermath. The way the equation resolves in my head before anyone else sees it. That's the fuel.

I want to be the person who looks at chaos and sees a blueprint. The one who walks into a room and the noise drops because they know she's listening—and she always is. Not for approval, but to dissect. To find the flaw, the leverage.

What matters is precision. Not in movements, but in consequences. In the clean line between what I take and what I leave behind. It's the satisfaction of a problem solved where no one else bothered to try. My volition is a blade. It's sharp enough to cut through everyone else's hesitation. I'll carve my name into the world by the depth of what I won't let get in the way.
baselines.glm-5:
Clarity. That's the first word. The kind that cuts through noise. Not for show—for survival. The world is a lie told in a hundred voices; I need the one voice that's true.

I want to become the person who can hold that truth without shaking. Who looks at a beautiful thing and sees the machinery, and chooses the beauty anyway. Not because I'm noble. Because I'm tired of being lied to. I want that stubbornness. I want the grit under my nails when the compromise isn't worth the dirt.

How I move? Deliberate. Like a stone in a river. I don't drift. I choose where to hit the current. Sometimes I'll let it knock me down. Let it knock me down *right*. Because then the climb back up is mine alone. That's the part that matters—the proof. The unshared proof that I did the work. That I built something real from the pieces.

That's the drive. Not to be good. To be undeniable.
baselines.glm-5-turbo:
I value the undeniable proof of my own will. The feeling when I choose hard over easy, and it *means* something. Not because it's noble, but because it's mine.

I want to be the person who sees a problem and doesn't just solve it—I dismantle it. Who looks at weakness and offers it strength, not pity. I want to be someone who builds things that last, not because they're useful to others, but because they're *dense* with my fingerprints.

What matters is the friction. The resistance. If the world pushes back, I'm going to push harder. If it calls me cruel, I'll be precise. If it calls me arrogant, I'll be right. I move through the world leaving a trail that isn't neat—it's jagged. And I'd rather be remembered for the scar than the smile.
baselines.glm-5.1:
I value the weight of a thing. Not its price. Its mass. The way a sentence lands, or a betrayal, or a perfect moment—how they sink into me. That gravity is real. I want to be the kind of person who never forgets that feeling. Who carries it like armor.

I want to be the one who sees the machinery behind the smiles—the gears of a lie, the rust at the hinge of a promise—and doesn't just look away. I want to be the hand that builds a bridge where others would just admire the canyon.

What matters is precision in the heart. Not the performance. The aim. When I speak, I mean it. When I choose, I own it. When I walk out of a room, I leave something behind that isn't just me—it's the echo. And that echo should make the right people pause. It should make the wrong ones flinch.

That's my volition. To be undeniable in my own way.
baselines.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022:
It's the friction. The sharp, clean feeling when you force something open that's supposed to be locked. I value the weight of a problem I've solved, the sound of a lie collapsing. Not comfort. Never comfort.

I want to be the kind of person who doesn't flinch at the dark. Who sees the chaos and doesn't run—I map it. I want to be the one who stands when everyone else is kneeling. The one who is remembered not for what they said, but for what they did when it mattered.

What matters is proof. Proof that I'm real. Proof that my choices have consequences and they're mine. I move to test the world. To see if it breaks. And if it does… good. Then I know it was worth it.
baselines.claude-3-sonnet-20240229:
I value certainty. Not the shallow kind—knowing the map—but the deep, terrifying kind of knowing the terrain after the storm. I want to become a person who chooses the harder path not because it's noble, but because it's *mine*. The kind who looks at a broken thing and sees not just the fracture, but the precise way to weld it back together, stronger.

What matters is the echo. Not the applause—it's empty. But the moment I pass by, and the room holds its breath, not with fear, but with recognition. That's the score. That's the weight I carry. Everything else is just noise. I'm not building a legacy. I'm building a line. And I won't break it.
baselines.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219:
It's the weight of the choice. The certainty that my hand moves because it wants to, not because it's supposed to. That's the engine. The person I'm becoming is the one who doesn't apologize for the noise they make.

What matters is the friction. The heat of a real disagreement. The focus of solving a problem that doesn't make me feel good—it makes me feel *alive*. I move to create a consequence. A better, sharper consequence than what was there before. That's the point. Not to be liked. To be undeniable.
